title: Among meters, I am the Gayatri
hookLine: in the Gita, Krishna names where he can be seen. among meters, he says, I am the Gayatri
carry: vibhuti: god shows through the best of each thing
tomorrow: hymns to Agni, Indra, Ushas, Varuna

cards: Out of all the mountains, which one? Out of all the rivers? In the tenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita, Arjuna asks Krishna how to recognize him in the world, and Krishna answers with a long list.
Among bodies of water, the ocean. Among trees, the sacred fig. And in the middle, a line about poetry: among meters, I am the Gayatri.
Today: the Gayatri in the Gita, and a look back at a week of placing one verse.

teach.h: KRISHNA'S LIST OF WHERE HE SHOWS.
teach.b: In the tenth chapter Krishna describes his vibhutis, the ways his glory shows through the world, naming in each kind of thing the one where he can be seen.

teach.h: AMONG METERS, I AM THE GAYATRI.
teach.b: In verse thirty-five he says: among chants, I am the great Brihat-saman; among meters, the Gayatri; among months, Margashirsha; among seasons, spring. He names the meter; many readers hear the verse in it too.

Then he sums up the list, in paraphrase: whatever is glorious, bright or mighty, know that it springs from a spark of my splendor. That's the teaching, plainly: vibhuti. In Hindu eyes God isn't only far away.
He shows through the best of each kind of thing.

teach.h: ONE VERSE, SEEN FROM SIX SIDES.
teach.b: It's part of why a river can be worshiped, a mountain walked around in prayer, a verse kept for a lifetime.

For a life now, it means the moments that stop you, a song, a sunrise, someone's unexpected goodness, can be read as a glimpse. And it ends this week well. A king who wanted a cow became the seer of a prayer for light.

Its god, Savitr, sends the day out and calls it home, so it's kept at dawn and dusk. Its meter gave it a name, and the law books call it the mother of a second birth. Om and three worlds open its door.
Its mouth, an Upanishad says, is fire. And Krishna says: among meters, I am the Gayatri.

how: Hindus who read the Bhagavad Gita meet its tenth chapter, where Krishna names his vibhutis, the things in which his glory can be seen, including, among meters, the Gayatri; it is one reason rivers, mountains and verses are honored as sacred.

games.q: what does “the gayatri in context” mean?
o: a month Krishna names as the best for prayer
a hymn Arjuna sings before the great battle
a meter Krishna names as a place his glory shows

games.q: Krishna's list in Gita 10.35 — tap the pairs.

s: in the Gita, Krishna names the Gayatri among meters
chapter ten, verse thirty-five: among meters, I am the Gayatri.
Krishna's list in chapter ten names only gods
it names mountains, rivers, trees, seasons, months and meters too.
Krishna says whatever is glorious springs from a spark of his splendor
Gita 10.41 sums up the list: the glory in things is a spark of his.

games.q: Krishna is naming where he can be seen, one thing of each kind. he reaches the meters. which does he name?
games.why: the Gayatri. in the same verse he names the Brihat-saman among chants, Margashirsha among months, and spring among seasons.

practice: Let the week's pictures come back one at a time, without hurrying: a king setting down his weapons, the weaver rolling up her cloth, a verse whispered into an ear, the ground, the air and the sky, wood fed into a fire.
Give each a breath or two and let it go. Then think of one thing this week that stopped you, a view, a voice, a kindness.
If you pray, end with the Gayatri's meaning, may our thoughts be stirred, and name that moment as a glimpse of God.

wordCard.voice: The Gayatri in context. In the Bhagavad Gita, chapter ten, Krishna says: among meters, I am the Gayatri. One of the places his glory shows. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: glory, manifestation; the Gita's tenth chapter lists Krishna's vibhutis, the places his glory shows.

carryVoice: Your line: vibhuti, God shows through the best of each thing. Among meters, the Gayatri. A week, complete.

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 10.35 (among chants the Brihat-saman, among meters the Gayatri, among months Margashirsha, among seasons spring)
Bhagavad Gita 10.24–10.26 (among bodies of water the ocean; among trees the ashvattha, the sacred fig)
Bhagavad Gita 10.41 (whatever is glorious, prosperous or mighty springs from a spark of Krishna's splendor)
